newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares head down after nine-day record run.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares head down after nine-day record run.

text.p: Egyptian share prices eased on Thursday for the first time in nine days as the market took a breather from racing to record highs and profit-taking set in.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index closed 0.89 points lower at 323.94, its first slip since the index shot to a record 288.89 points on December 29.
"The market is stabilising and its becoming a buyers market -- there weren't many buyers with such prices," said broker Mohammed Hanafi of Megavest.
Major bourse player Medinet Nasr Housing and Development were among the worst hit by profit-taking, with shares falling 19.99 pounds to 400.00.
Heliopolis Housing and Development, another market shaker, also tumbled 28.55 to 542.45 as the February deadline for a 10-for-one share split loomed.
"Investors are selling now when the prices are good before they fall as they naturally will after the split," Hanafi said.

Rumours of another impending share split by Commercial International Bank (CIB) triggered 2.9 million pounds worth of trading in the stock but share price remained unchanged at 600 pounds as stock market officials maintained their price cap, brokers said.
"Maybe the bourse officials are afraid that the prices will fall too much too soon and that's why they have the ceiling in place," a broker said.

Thursday's overall turnover was a healthy 69.57 million pounds ($20.46 million) boosted by a handful of deals in Eipico/Egyptian International Pharmaceutical Industries worth 19.95 million pounds. Brokers said the one of the firm's main shareholders was selling a stake to another.
Mutual funds also scooped up millions of pounds worth of milling shares but failed to increase many prices of the popular stocks.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills fell 4.25 to 89.00 in trading worth 4.12 million pounds while Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 1.89 pounds lower at 68.20 on a 3.87 million pound turnover.
The CMAindex for openly traded firms rose to 514.11 points from 510.39 on Wednesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms slipped to 220.56 points from 222.55.
Out of 81 shares traded, 30 advanced, 27 declined and the other 24 ended the day unchanged.
